summary.intent: Fix the release gate CI action that was unnecessarily blocking a release-please PR containing only a minor CI workflow change, where neither the web app nor desktop app had changed.
summary.outcome: Release gate was fixed to add web change detection and make both Web/Desktop E2E gates conditional on actual app changes. A second fix was applied to ci-e2e.yml so that workflow_dispatch triggers always run E2E (bypassing change detection), and the retrigger-release-gate job also fires on dispatch.

repo: The repo is a monorepo (FSM1/cipher-box) with web, desktop, and multiple packages (crypto, api-client, sdk-core, sdk) under packages/
release-gate.yml gates merges of release-please PRs by requiring Web E2E and Desktop E2E to have passed for the commits being released
ci-e2e.yml uses dorny/paths-filter to detect whether web or desktop changed, then conditionally runs E2E jobs
The retrigger-release-gate job in ci-e2e.yml automatically re-runs the release gate on release-please PRs after E2E completes
Branch protection required status checks are managed via GitHub API, not in workflow files
Cross-Language Vector Parity job has an if-condition that only runs on desktop/src changes — could become a merge blocker for PRs that skip it
PR #402 (Node.js 24 Actions update) touched both desktop-e2e.yml and web-e2e.yml, which triggered both E2E flags in the release gate

code.finding: dorny/paths-filter uses github.event.before as base; on workflow_dispatch this is empty so it falls back to HEAD~1, causing both web and desktop to be detected as unchanged and E2E jobs to be skipped

web-e2e and desktop-e2e jobs already had `|| github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'` conditions, but this was ineffective because detect-changes itself skips the filter on dispatch, outputting false
WEB_PATTERNS uses packages/ prefix which covers all downstream dependencies (crypto, api-client, sdk-core, sdk) via grep -Fq, mirroring ci-e2e.yml's web filter but excluding ci-e2e.yml itself

workflow: When dorny/paths-filter is used for change detection, workflow_dispatch events need explicit handling to force all-changed behavior, since there's no meaningful 'before' SHA
CI orchestrator workflow files (ci-e2e.yml) should not be included in app-specific path patterns — their change doesn't mean the app changed, and including them causes false E2E requirements
Manually triggering a workflow via workflow_dispatch to unblock a release gate is a valid workaround, but requires the dispatch path to be correctly wired up first

friction: First fix (PR #407) did not fully resolve the issue — web-e2e.yml and desktop-e2e.yml being in their respective patterns meant the Node.js 24 Actions PR still triggered both flags
User had to investigate a second failing release gate run after the first fix was merged, discovering the root cause was a different PR (#402)
Manually triggered ci-e2e.yml run failed spectacularly because workflow_dispatch change detection was broken — the fix for this was not in place before the manual trigger was attempted
An uncommitted branch (fix/release-gate-workflow-patterns) was created and then abandoned mid-commit when the user redirected approach, requiring cleanup
open_items: Cross-Language Vector Parity is now a required check but only runs conditionally on desktop/src changes — PRs that don't touch those paths may be blocked by a pending/skipped check

The release-please PR (#406) may still need the ci-e2e.yml dispatch fix to land and a fresh E2E run to complete before the release gate passes — outcome of the final ci-e2e.yml fix was not confirmed in the transcript
No automated test validates that workflow_dispatch correctly forces E2E runs — relies on manual verification after deployment
